relations.definition: A relationship where an organization provides financial or institutional support for an activity.
relations.embedding_query_text: sponsored_by: A relationship where an organization provides financial or institutional support for an activity.

instances: Ebola treatments trial in DR Congo -> World Health Organization

chosen_property.label: sponsor
chosen_property.justification: The 'sponsor' property from schema.org has a domain including Event and a range of Organization, which matches the instance 'Ebola treatments trial in DR Congo' (Event) --> 'World Health Organization' (Organization).

candidates.label: sponsor
candidates.comment: A support relation between an entity (creative work, event, grant, study, organization, or person) and the person or organization providing financial or other backing. Also called "funded by", "supported by", "patron", "underwritten by". Examples: "The event has sponsor Acme Corp", "The medical study's sponsor is the NIH", "This artist has sponsor a private foundation."

candidates.label: funder
candidates.comment: A funder relation between a creative work, event, grant, organization, or person and the organization or person providing financial support or sponsorship. Also called: sponsor, benefactor, financial supporter. Examples: "Art Exhibition" funder "National Endowment for the Arts", "Research Project" funder "NIH", "Charity Event" funder "Local Bank". Distinct from fundedItem, which is the item receiving funding.

candidates.label: funding
candidates.comment: A funding relation between a biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product and the grant that provides its direct or indirect financial support. Also called: grant received, sponsorship, financial support. Examples: "Cancer Research Project" funding "NIH Grant R01", "Local Theater Production" funding "Arts Council Grant", "Student Scholarship Program" funding "University Endowment Grant". Distinct from funder, which is the entity providing the funding.

candidates.label: fundedItem
candidates.comment: A funded item relation between a grant and the biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product that receives direct or indirect funding or sponsorship. Also called: grant recipient, sponsored item, supported entity. Examples: "Research Grant" funded item "Cancer Research Project", "Arts Grant" funded item "Local Theater Production", "Educational Grant" funded item "Student Scholarship Program". Distinct from funding, which is the grant itself.

candidates.label: provider
candidates.comment: A provision relation between an action, work, program, or service and the organization or person that supplies or performs it. Also called supplied by, performed by, offered by, produced by. Examples: "A parcel delivery is provided by FedEx.", "A financial incentive is provided by the government.", "A medical service is provided by Dr. Smith."

candidates.label: hasSponsorshipOffer
candidates.comment: A sponsorship offer relation between an event and an offer to sponsor it. Also called sponsorship opportunity, sponsor package, call for sponsors. Examples: "An event has a sponsorship offer for corporate partners.", "The conference has a sponsorship offer with different tiers.", "This festival includes a sponsorship offer.". Distinct from hasParticipationOffer, which is an offer to participate in the event.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: endorsee
candidates.comment: An endorsee relation between an endorse action and the person or organization being supported. Also called "supported entity", "beneficiary", "recipient of endorsement". Examples: "Endorse action endorsee 'Candidate A'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Charity B'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Product C'". Distinct from endorsers, which are the people or organizations providing the endorsement.

candidates.label: eligibleWithSupplier
candidates.comment: An eligible with supplier relation between a financial incentive and the organization that supplies the incentivized item or service. Also called "supplier partner", "incentive provider", "valid with retailer". Examples: "Rebate eligibleWithSupplier 'Utility Company X'", "Discount eligibleWithSupplier 'Electronics Store Y'", "Grant eligibleWithSupplier 'Solar Panel Installer Z'".

candidates.label: publisher
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a creative work or financial incentive and the organization or person that publishes it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book has a publisher 'Penguin Random House'.", "A research paper has a publisher 'Nature Publishing Group'.", "A financial incentive has a publisher 'Government Agency'.". Distinct from publishedBy, which refers to the agent of a specific publication event.

relations.definition: A relationship where an organization or individual leads the planning and execution of an activity.
relations.embedding_query_text: coordinated_by: A relationship where an organization or individual leads the planning and execution of an activity.

Ebola treatments trial in DR Congo -> University of Oxford

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: sourceOrganization
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a creative work and the organization on whose behalf its creator was working. Also called "commissioning organization", "producing organization", "organization behind", "publisher organization". Examples: "The research paper's sourceOrganization was MIT", "The documentary's sourceOrganization was BBC", "This report's sourceOrganization is the World Health Organization."

candidates.label: agent
candidates.comment: An agent relation between an action and the organization or person who directly performs or drives it. Also called performer, doer, initiator, actor. Examples: "A 'write book' action's agent is 'John Doe'.", "A 'deliver package' action's agent is 'Delivery Service Inc'."

candidates.label: parentOrganization
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between an organization and the larger organization it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is a division of, is a subsidiary of, is part of. Examples: Google is a parent organization of YouTube. A local branch is a parent organization of its national headquarters. A department is a parent organization of its university. Distinct from subOrganization, which points from a larger organization to its smaller components.

candidates.label: followee
candidates.comment: A followee relation between a follow action and the person or organization that is being followed. Also called: followed entity, subject of follow, target of follow. Examples: "User A follows User B" followee "User B", "Fan follows Band X" followee "Band X", "Journalist follows News Organization Y" followee "News Organization Y". Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: gameLocation
candidates.comment: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".

candidates.label: homeLocation
candidates.comment: A home location relation between a person and their residential contact point or place. Also called residence, dwelling, home address. Examples: "A person has a home location in London.", "Her home location is a specific address.", "The individual's home location is a contact point."

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: workLocation
candidates.comment: A work location relation between a person and a contact point or place, identifying where the person performs their professional duties. Also called employment location, office address, workplace. Examples: John workLocation MainOffice, Jane workLocation RemoteHome, CompanyEmployee workLocation BranchOffice. Distinct from homeLocation, which is a person's residential address.

candidates.label: globalLocationNumber
candidates.comment: A global location number relation between an organization, person, or place and its unique 13-digit GLN identifier. Also called: GLN, International Location Number, ILN. Examples: "Acme Corp Warehouse" global location number "1234567890123", "Hospital Main Campus" global location number "9876543210987", "Distribution Center X" global location number "1122334455667".

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess
candidates.comment: A biological function relation between a biochemical entity and the biological process it participates in. Also called participates in process, role in biological process, contributes to process. Examples: A protein is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'cell division'. An enzyme is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'metabolism'. A hormone is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'growth regulation'.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: program
candidates.comment: An association between a program membership and the specific member program it belongs to. Also called part of program, associated program, membership program. Examples: "A loyalty card membership is part of the 'Star Alliance Gold' program.", "A gym membership is part of the 'Premium Fitness' program.", "A frequent flyer membership is part of the 'SkyMiles' program.". Distinct from programName, which is the textual name of the program.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: infectiousAgent
candidates.comment: A causative agent relation between an infectious disease and the specific microorganism or pathogen that causes it. Also called causative organism, pathogen, disease agent, etiological agent. Examples: Influenza has an infectiousAgent of 'Influenza virus'. Tuberculosis has an infectiousAgent of 'Mycobacterium tuberculosis'. Malaria has an infectiousAgent of 'Plasmodium falciparum'. Distinct from infectiousAgentClass, which specifies the *type* of agent (e.g., bacteria, virus).

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: copyrightNotice
candidates.comment: A textual declaration relation between a creative work and the statement describing its copyright aspects. Also called: copyright statement, copyright declaration, copyright text. Examples: "My Novel" copyright notice "© 2023 John Doe", "Company Website" copyright notice "Copyright 2023 Example Corp. All Rights Reserved.", "Academic Paper" copyright notice "Published under CC BY 4.0 license". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which identifies the entity owning the copyright.

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

relations.definition: A relationship where a statement or claim is attributed to a source.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: creditedTo
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a music release and the group or artist it is credited to, if different from the primary artist. Also called: attributed to, release credit, presented by. Examples: "Album 'Red and Blue'" credited to "Stefani Germanotta Band", "Single 'X'" credited to "The Session Musicians", "Soundtrack" credited to "Various Artists".

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

relations.definition: A relationship indicating a connection between two entities without a direct causal or hierarchical link.
relations.embedding_query_text: linked_to: A relationship indicating a connection between two entities without a direct causal or hierarchical link.

candidates.label: linkRelationship
candidates.comment: A link relationship type relation between a link role and its descriptive text. Also called: hyperlink relation, link type, relationship attribute. Examples: "LinkRole linkRelationship 'nofollow'", "LinkRole linkRelationship 'alternate'", "LinkRole linkRelationship 'canonical'".

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: inverseOf
candidates.comment: A property relationship indicating that two properties describe the same association between entities but in opposite directions. Also called reciprocal property, opposite property, reverse property. Examples: The 'alumni' property is an inverseOf 'alumniOf'. The 'parent' property is an inverseOf 'child'. The 'employee' property is an inverseOf 'worksFor'.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: relatedLink
candidates.comment: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."

candidates.label: follows
candidates.comment: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.

candidates.label: geoDisjoint
candidates.comment: A geo disjoint relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places have no points in common and are entirely disconnected. Also called: separate from, not overlapping, unconnected. Examples: "Country 'USA'" geo disjoint "Country 'China'", "Island 'Hawaii'" geo disjoint "Continent 'Europe'", "Building 'A'" geo disjoint "Building 'B'". Distinct from geoIntersects, which has at least one point in common.

candidates.label: subOrganization
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a parent organization and a smaller organization that is a part of it, such as a subsidiary. Also called "subsidiary", "division", "affiliated organization", "part of organization".
